2027-01-03.title: Second Sunday after Yaldo
readings: The boy Samuel grows before the Lord
They shall mount up with wings like eagles
Here is the Lamb of God
2027-01-03.alt: Season of Yaldo–Denho. Denho, the Baptism of our Lord, is on Wednesday 6 January.
2027-01-03.verse: Here is the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world!
theo: Between Yaldo and Denho the Church listens to John the Baptist. He sees Jesus coming and cries: “Here is the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world!” The Child of Bethlehem is the Lamb who will be offered for us. John adds: “I myself have seen and have testified that this is the Son of God.” Christmas joy is joined to the purpose of Christ's coming: to take away sin.

In the evening Gospel John is very practical. The crowds ask, “What then should we do?” He answers: “Whoever has two coats must share with anyone who has none; and whoever has food must do likewise.” Tax collectors must be honest; soldiers must not extort. Conversion is not only a feeling; it bears fruit in the way we use money, power and possessions.

The Old Testament readings show children growing before God: Joseph loved by his father and given a long robe; the boy Samuel growing “in the presence of the LORD”, his mother bringing him a little robe each year. Hebrews remembers Moses, who chose “to share ill-treatment with the people of God rather than to enjoy the fleeting pleasures of sin”.

Isaiah gives the promise for the new year: “Those who wait for the LORD shall renew their strength, they shall mount up with wings like eagles, they shall run and not be weary.” Those who follow the Lamb do not run on their own strength.
conn: The Passover lamb (Exodus 12) and the servant “like a lamb that is led to the slaughter” (Isaiah 53:7) are fulfilled in Jesus, the Lamb of God (John 1:29; Revelation 5:6).
Joseph's robe and Samuel's little robe are signs of a parent's love; in Baptism we are clothed with Christ (Galatians 3:27).
“Let us love, not in word or speech, but in truth and action” (1 John 3:18) is the same lesson as John's “two coats”.
Moses refused Pharaoh's palace for God's people; Christ left heaven's glory for us.
altar: Before Holy Communion the priest raises the holy Mysteries; in many liturgies we hear John's words: “Behold the Lamb of God.” The One John pointed to by the Jordan is the One we receive at the altar.
outline: Ask: what did we receive at Christmas? What did we give?
The Child of Yaldo is the Lamb who takes away sin.
Two coats, honest work, no extortion: conversion in practice.
Joseph, Samuel, Moses: let children grow in God's presence.
New strength for the new year for those who wait on the Lord.
“Behold the Lamb; and share your second coat.”
live: Give away one good item of clothing or food this week to someone who needs it.
Check one area of your work or business for honesty and fairness.
Come to the Denho Qurbono on Wednesday and renew your baptismal promises.
fathers: One Lamb died for all, to gather the whole flock of humanity to God the Father; one for all, that all might be subject to God (Commentary on John, Book 2).
On “whoever has two coats”: mercy is the fullness of the virtues; it is required of all, rich and poor, according to what each has (Exposition of the Gospel of Luke 2).
magis: John the Baptist pointed to Jesus as the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world: the Suffering Servant and the Paschal Lamb.
Interior conversion is expressed in fasting, prayer and almsgiving, reconciliation, and care for the poor.
Love for the poor; giving to the needy is a work of justice.
saints: 3 Jan: St Kuriakose Elias Chavara. 6 Jan (Wednesday): Denho, the Baptism of our Lord; Holy Qurbono for the people. 7 Jan: Exaltation of St John the Baptist. 8 Jan: Mar Stephanos (St Stephen), the first martyr.
2027-01-03.prayer: Lord Jesus, Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world, have mercy on us. Make our conversion bear fruit in sharing, honesty and love, and renew our strength in this new year, that we may run and not be weary. Amen.

quick: The Child of Bethlehem is the Lamb of God.
Conversion bears fruit: share your second coat.
Those who wait for the Lord renew their strength.
2027-01-03.action: Give away one good item of clothing or food this week.
2027-01-03.question: What is my “second coat” that someone else needs?
2027-01-03.special: Second Sunday after Yaldo. Announce Denho on Wednesday 6 January, a day of obligation.
illus: After Christmas many Kerala homes have cupboards full of new clothes. One parish asks families to bring one good garment to church on the Sunday after Christmas for the poor. The pile at the door is John the Baptist's sermon in action.

family.explain: John the Baptist said: if you have two shirts, give one away. And he pointed to Jesus and said: “Look, the Lamb of God!”
family.intention: We pray for people who are cold or hungry this January.
family.ask: Ask: “What can our family share this week?”

kidsaint: A priest from Kainakary in Kerala who started schools beside churches so that every child could learn, founded religious congregations and printed books. Lesson: learning is a gift from God; use it to help others.
term: John the Baptist's name for Jesus (John 1:29). It recalls the Passover lamb and the Suffering Servant of Isaiah: Jesus gives his life to take away the sin of the world.
termMore: The days from Christmas to the Baptism of the Lord unfold one mystery: God revealed in Christ, to the shepherds, to the Magi, and at the Jordan.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Lamb of God, John pointed to you so that all might follow you. Open our eyes to see you as we gather. Amen.
share: Here is the Lamb of God (John 1:29). How do I point others to Jesus?
Whoever has two coats must share with anyone who has none (Luke 3:11). What can I share this week?
Moses chose to share ill-treatment with the people of God (Hebrews 11:25). What comfort am I willing to give up for God?
pm.resp: Lamb of God, have mercy on us.
interc: For the Church, that she may point all people to Christ.
For the poor who lack clothing and food.
For those tempted by passing pleasures.
For the tired and discouraged, that they may renew their strength in God (Isaiah 40:31).
For our group, that we may share generously.
pm.close: Father, your Son is the Lamb who takes away the sin of the world. Make us his witnesses and generous to the poor. Through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, we are still in the light of Christmas, and today John the Baptist points to the Child of Bethlehem and says: “Here is the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world!” The baby in the manger came for a purpose: to give his life for us, as the Passover lamb was given for Israel.

In the evening Gospel the crowds ask John: “What then should we do?” His answer is very simple. “Whoever has two coats must share with anyone who has none; whoever has food must do likewise.” To tax collectors: be honest. To soldiers: do not extort. Conversion is not a beautiful feeling; it is a changed way of using what we have.

After Christmas many of us have more than enough: new clothes, sweets, gifts. John asks: where is your second coat? Who needs it? Our readings also show children growing up close to God: Samuel growing in the presence of the Lord, his mother bringing him a little robe each year. Let us help our children grow like that.

And as the new year begins, Isaiah promises: “Those who wait for the Lord shall renew their strength, they shall mount up with wings like eagles.” On Wednesday we celebrate Denho, the Baptism of the Lord. Come, renew your own baptism, and follow the Lamb. Amen.
kids: Children, John the Baptist was Jesus' cousin. When he saw Jesus coming, he said: “Look! The Lamb of God!” He meant that Jesus came to take away all our sins.
People asked John: “What should we do?” He said: “If you have two shirts, give one to someone who has none.”
Do you have a toy or a shirt you could share? Let's say: “Like John, I will share!”

intro: John the Baptist points away from himself to Jesus: “Here is the Lamb of God.” He also tells ordinary people how to prepare for him: by concrete repentance in daily life.

sub: Isaiah saw a silent Servant led like a lamb to the slaughter.
John recognises Jesus as the Lamb who takes away the sin of the world.
The Church calls Christ the Lamb in her liturgy; in the Holy Qurbono we receive the Lamb who was sacrificed for us.
q: Like a lamb that is led to the slaughter, and like a sheep that before its shearers is silent, so he did not open his mouth.
Here is the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world!
points.apply: Look at the Holy Mysteries at the elevation and say in your heart: “Lamb of God, have mercy on me.”

sub: The crowds ask: “What then should we do?”
John's answers are practical: share your coat and food; collect only what is just; do not threaten or accuse falsely.
Isaiah too: cease to do evil, learn to do good, defend the orphan and the widow.
q: Cease to do evil, learn to do good; seek justice, rescue the oppressed, defend the orphan, plead for the widow.
And the crowds asked him, “What then should we do?” In reply he said to them, “Whoever has two coats must share with anyone who has none; and whoever has food must do likewise.”
points.apply: Give away one good garment or one day's food to someone in need this week.

sub: The boy Samuel grew in favour with God and people while serving in the Temple.
John saw the Spirit descend and testified: “This is the Son of God.”
Every Christian is called to grow in faith and to bear witness, not to himself, but to Christ.
q: Now the boy Samuel continued to grow both in stature and in favor with the LORD and with the people.
And I myself have seen and have testified that this is the Son of God.
points.apply: Speak of Jesus simply to one person this week: what he means to you.

concl: John's whole life is a finger pointing to Christ.
Let our lives too say to others: “Behold the Lamb of God.”
2027-01-03.resolve: Pray each night this week: “Lamb of God, who takes away the sins of the world, have mercy on us.”
